solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hartebeest, perhaps, may cause worker to run away

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
to elope is to run away secretly to marry

explanation.surface: A startled hartebeest could make a labourer flee.
explanation.definitionFit: The hartebeest is a large African grazing animal of the antelope family, so it is an example, flagged by 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Reddish-brown and gold stream

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a burn is a Scottish stream

explanation.surface: A coppery-coloured and golden brook.
explanation.walkthrough: BURN is a Scots and northern English word for a small stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn names a reddish-brown shade, usually of hair.

clue.text: Play: shrewd, but flawed by excessive complexity

definitions.meaning: a comedy by Ostrovsky, known in English by this title

definitions.text: shrewd, but flawed by excessive complexity
definitions.meaning: describing someone whose cleverness overreaches itself

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being so clever as to become irritating or self-defeating; it is also the English title of an Ostrovsky comedy.

clue.text: There's no mixer in cocktail, one remembered

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cocktail without a mixer was a memorable one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No mixer' looks like a neat drink; it means a person who does not mix socially. The letters sit across cocktaiL ONE Remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps to themselves and avoids company is unsociable, not a mixer.

clue.text: Cut in wages may make one very nervous

indicators.note: in places the word for cut inside the word for wages

parts.note: pay is wages
a nick is a small cut

explanation.surface: A pay cut can make anyone anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Panicky means prone to sudden fear, highly anxious.

clue.text: Cause to stumble at university, on excursion

indicators.note: in this across clue one piece is placed on, that is after, the other

parts.note: a trip is an excursion or outing
up means in residence at a university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A student on a day out somehow causes someone to fall.
explanation.walkthrough: UP for 'at university' is a British usage: students go up to Oxford or Cambridge and come down when they leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip someone up is to make them stumble, literally or by catching them in an error.

clue.text: Lying down, ugly bum coming in late

indicators.note: coming in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in 'the late news'

indicators.note: ugly suggests the letters are deformed into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone with an unattractive backside arrives late and lies down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ugly' is the anagram signal; 'late' means recently, not tardy, and the shuffled backside goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent means reclining or lying down.

clue.text: Capital, the American bishop in hit play

indicators.note: in places the string of pieces inside the word for hit

parts.note: to pound is to hit repeatedly
Rome is the capital of Italy
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Italy's capital, the US and a bishop in a successful play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like a hit show but is POUND. Aeschylus' tragedy shows the Titan chained for giving fire to mankind.
explanation.definitionFit: A classical Greek tragedy, traditionally attributed to Aeschylus.

clue.text: Hill damaged a pit lane

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A racing circuit's service road has been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the seven hills of Rome, the site of the imperial palaces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palatine is one of the seven hills on which ancient Rome was built.

clue.text: Poet, bachelor, arguing about name

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for arguing goes round the letter for name

parts.note: rowing (rhymes with 'cowing') is quarrelling

explanation.surface: A single poet quarrels over what someone is called.
explanation.walkthrough: Here ROWING is the British word for quarrelling, rhyming with 'cowing', not the boating sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning, and Elizabeth Barrett Browning, were celebrated Victorian poets.

clue.text: Group in coach

definitions.meaning: a group, especially of fish, as in a ... of whales or a ... of thought
to coach is to train or instruct someone

explanation.definitionFit: A school is a gathering of fish or a body of like-minded people, and as a verb it means to teach or train.

clue.text: Prophet captured by Grandma Moses

indicators.note: captured by means the letters are held within the following words

explanation.surface: A prophet is painted by the American folk artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Grandma Moses was a famous American folk painter; 'captured by' points to the letters spanning grandmA MOSes.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a minor prophet of the Old Testament, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Monarch — one responsible for a line?

definitions.meaning: a monarch is a sovereign who reigns
a measuring stick is what draws a straight line

explanation.surface: A king answers for a dynasty's line of succession.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign rules, and the straight-edged drawing tool also used for measuring is likewise called by this word.

clue.text: Representative feeding domestic pet cheese

indicators.note: one piece feeding into another goes inside it, like food into a mouth

parts.note: the cat is the commonest domestic pet
a Member of Parliament is a representative

explanation.surface: An MP gives their household pet some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representative' is a Member of Parliament, and 'feeding' puts that member inside the pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft creamy French variety from Normandy, a classic example of cheese.

clue.text: A change required to protect one enclosure for birds

indicators.note: to protect is to surround, so the word for change wraps round the numeral

parts.note: to vary is to change
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Some alteration is needed to safeguard a single pen for birds.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large cage or building in which birds are kept.

clue.text: Acknowledging a call involving bad news

indicators.note: involving means the pair takes the anagrammed letters inside

parts.note: a ring is a telephone call

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of news are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Picking up the phone when it brings bad tidings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' scrambles the news, which then sits between A and the call.
explanation.definitionFit: Answering is replying to or acknowledging something, such as a letter or a greeting.

clue.text: Boy — he spent unwisely

indicators.note: unwisely suggests the letters of the phrase are carelessly scattered

explanation.surface: A young man has wasted his money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwisely' turns HE SPENT into a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so any boy so called; crosswords often define names this way.

clue.text: By entrance to shore, see tourist, one removing clothes

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

parts.note: a tripper is a day-tripper, a tourist

explanation.surface: Near the path to the beach, watch a holidaymaker undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIPPER is a British word for a holidaymaker on a day trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper is someone who takes off clothes, often as entertainment; the word also names a paint remover.

clue.text: Goes home and goes to bed

parts.note: to turn is to go or become, as milk turns sour
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Someone heads back and retires for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes home' pretends to be one phrase meaning returning; it is two pieces, 'Goes' as becomes and 'home' as not out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb is an idiom for retiring for the night.

clue.text: Almost dark? Almost

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut from the word

parts.note: night is the dark hours

explanation.surface: Is it nearly dark? Very nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' does two jobs in two places: the first cuts the last letter, the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old word for near or nearly.

clue.text: Pulled up solicitor, annoyed

indicators.note: pulled up reads as the word up being pulled round, turned the other way

parts.note: the word up itself
a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor in the literal sense

explanation.surface: A lawyer was stopped short and became irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulled' turns UP into PU. A solicitor in Britain is a kind of lawyer, but here it means one who solicits, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put out is an idiom meaning offended or irritated.

clue.text: Chatter about the Spanish clergyman

indicators.note: about means the chatter goes around the article

parts.note: to prate is to chatter foolishly
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Gossip about the Spanish churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a high-ranking clergyman, such as a bishop.

clue.text: Runs after penniless agent

indicators.note: after places the abbreviation for runs following the word for penniless

parts.note: broke means having no money
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An agent chases a destitute client.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker is an agent who buys and sells on behalf of others.

clue.text: Brown is one of its members, climber some distance behind

definitions.text: Brown is one of its members

indicators.note: behind places the distance after the plant

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
a league is an old unit of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: Someone named Brown belongs, with a mountaineer trailing far back.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown is Brown University in Rhode Island, not a person or a colour; it belongs to the group of eight elite north-eastern US universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown University is one of the eight members of this athletic conference of old American universities.

clue.text: Flowing robes, muted in colour

indicators.note: flowing suggests the letters drift loosely into a new order

explanation.surface: Billowing gowns in subdued shades.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober colours are restrained and dull rather than bright.

clue.text: Colander is put up by girl

indicators.note: by means beside, so the girl's name follows
in a down clue, put up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A kitchen strainer is hung up by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns IS into SI, with EVE beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sieve is a mesh utensil for straining, like a colander.

clue.text: Cool about wearing tartan

indicators.note: the tartan is worn around the abbreviation, so it goes outside

parts.note: plaid is tartan cloth
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Unruffled in a kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and unexcitable, as a cool temperament is.

clue.text: Ineffectual type made out, coming into fortune

indicators.note: one piece comes into, goes inside, the other

parts.note: luck is fortune

indicators.note: out means the letters of made are put out of order

explanation.surface: A useless person who was identified while inheriting money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made out' looks like 'identified', but 'out' is the anagram signal on 'made'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a weak or ineffective person, or an official serving out time after losing power.

clue.text: Say no? Good for son finding sanctuary

indicators.note: Good for son means one letter takes the place of the other

parts.note: to refuse is to say no

explanation.surface: A son who turns things down finds a safe haven.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge is a place of shelter or safety, which is what sanctuary means.

clue.text: One on team put back to guard goal

indicators.note: to guard is to surround, so the word for put back goes round the word for goal

parts.note: to defer is to postpone, put back
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A player was postponed to protect the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' suggests football's net, but it is END in the sense of an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A player whose role is to defend, a member of a sports team.
